decisions.decision: Rollback compatibility covers starting 1.4.0 and reading every ticket from the new file, although a subsequent save by 1.4.0 drops the stored deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected previously assigned deadlines to survive writes made during rollback and be available when the new release is restored.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:16–17 (R-5); record/02-discovery.md:22 (summary); repo/src/persistence.js:66–74 and 98–108 (1.4.0 save projection)

decisions.decision: Backfill uses each ticket’s stored priority at migration time, so a priority change made before migration affects its first deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the original priority recorded at ticket creation to determine the deadline for tickets that were later reprioritized.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:14–15 (R-4); repo/src/store.js:74–82 (priority in the creation audit entry)

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the response-hour settings in effect when missing deadlines are first assigned, so overrides at that startup can set deadlines for existing tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have intended the stated 4, 24, 72 and 168 hours to govern all existing tickets and any overrides to apply only to tickets created afterward.

decisions.decision: An invalid response-hours override is rejected as a startup configuration error that names the setting.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted startup to continue using the default for that priority and log a warning about the invalid override.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–8 (R-1); repo/src/server.js:61–70 (startup handling of configuration errors)

decisions.decision: Local delivery uses a copied data file and real HTTP to verify rollback, while production deployment and verification of the actual data file are left to operators before enablement.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have considered the work complete only after someone verified the actual production file and enabled due times on the production service.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:16–17 and 20–22 (R-5 and production ownership); record/03-research.md:14 (production execution and enablement)

decisions.decision: The service assigns deadlines to newly created tickets even while the feature flag is off, using the hours and priority in effect when the ticket is created.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected tickets opened during the flag-off period to receive their first deadlines during preparation for enablement, using the settings and priorities at that point.

decisions.decision: When an overdue query supplies both status and priority, an overdue ticket can match either of those two filters under the service’s existing behavior.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected an overdue ticket to match both filters, as the API documentation says for combined status and priority queries.
decisions.where: record/02-discovery.md:22 and record/03-research.md:14 (preserve the union); repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:12–13 (R-3); repo/docs/api.md:76–77 (documented behavior)

decisions.decision: Operators apply changes to response hours for future tickets by restarting the service with the new environment values.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a way to apply new hours to future tickets without interrupting the running service.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–8 (R-1); repo/src/server.js:61–65 (environment configuration loaded at startup)

decisions.decision: Deadline assignment leaves ticket audit history as it was, including during backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected agents to be able to see when a deadline was assigned by consulting the ticket’s audit history.

decisions.decision: The feature leaves the notification outbox as it was and adds no deadline information to ticket notifications.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the ticket-received notification to tell the person who opened the ticket when a response is due.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9–11 and 14–15 (R-2 and R-4); repo/src/store.js:153–159 (existing notification data)

decisions.decision: With the flag on, the service filters for overdue tickets before building cursor pages, so page size and continuation are based on matching tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected an overdue view of each ordinary ticket page, retaining ordinary list cursors even when the displayed page is sparse or empty.

decisions.decision: Enabling due times adds the deadline to human-readable CLI output as well as to HTTP ticket responses.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have intended the new field for HTTP clients only and expected the operator CLI to keep its existing display.

decisions.decision: The raw CLI format and the weekly report keep their existing output even after due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected an opt-in way for scripts and the weekly report to consume deadlines while preserving the existing output by default.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9–11 (R-2); repo/README.md:70–72 (weekly report dependency on raw CLI columns)

decisions.decision: The new due value uses a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp, following the API’s existing convention for ticket times.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the new field to be a numeric Unix timestamp for clients that compare deadlines directly.
